newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends sharply down in technical slide.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends sharply down in technical slide.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed sharply down in technically-driven speculative selling and an absence of mill buying, dealers said.
They noted long liquidation and additional selling once the most-active March contract fell below 75.00 cents.
Volume was estimated at a moderate 14,000 lots.
The most-active March contract ended 1.30 cent lower at 74.08 cents per pound, traded 75.40 to 74.00 cents. The back months finished 1.12 to 0.22 lower.

Today's weekly export and sales report may have added weight to the move. While the report, pegging new sales at 100,700 bakes for the week ended Dec 26 was not negative, it did not contribute any bullish news to an already dull market, analysts said.

They viewed today's close near the day's lows was as particularly bullish on a Friday and ahead of the annual industry-wide meeting next week. Nearly 6,000 cotton industry members are expected to attend the Beltwide Cotton Conference Jan 7-10 in New Orleans.
